patient.name: Marjorie Delacroix
patient.chief_complaint: Burning pain in both feet and lower legs, severe at night, for 18 months
patient.hpi: Marjorie Delacroix is a 52-year-old career diplomat with an 18-month history of progressively worsening neuropathic pain in her bilateral feet and lower legs. The pain is burning and lancinating in quality, significantly worse at night (allodynia to bedsheets), and interferes severely with her sleep. She has been unable to tolerate most footwear. She rates the pain as 8/10 on average and 10/10 at night. She has had several overseas postings, most recently 3 years in West Africa (2019-2022) and 18 months in South Asia (2022-2023). She received multiple vaccinations prior to posting including rabies series, meningococcal, typhoid, hepatitis A/B, and yellow fever. She has completed multiple antibiotic and antimalarial prophylaxis courses including dapsone, chloroquine, mefloquine, and a 9-month course of leflunomide for rheumatoid arthritis diagnosed 4 years ago. She takes methotrexate 15 mg weekly and leflunomide 20 mg daily for RA. Her current rheumatologist noted that her RA is in remission. She is very concerned that her medications may be causing nerve damage. She notes her symptoms began approximately 6 months after starting leflunomide. She has no diabetes and no alcohol use. Her prior neurologist attributed symptoms to 'stress' after NCS was interpreted as normal 1 year ago — she brings a copy of that NCS for review.

report.summary: NCS/EMG WITHIN NORMAL LIMITS FOR LARGE FIBER FUNCTION. This explains the prior NCS labeled 'normal' — standard NCS tests only large myelinated fibers (A-beta). Small fiber neuropathy (unmyelinated C fibers and thinly myelinated A-delta fibers) is INVISIBLE to standard NCS. The patient's clinical presentation of burning pain, allodynia, temperature loss with preserved reflexes and intact vibration/proprioception is the textbook phenotype of SMALL FIBER NEUROPATHY.

emg.summary: NCS/EMG entirely normal — no evidence of large fiber neuropathy. This is expected and DOES NOT exclude neuropathy. Small fiber neuropathy requires skin punch biopsy for IENFD or corneal confocal microscopy for diagnosis.

report.overall_impression: NORMAL LARGE FIBER NCS. Small fiber neuropathy cannot be evaluated by standard NCS. Skin punch biopsy for intraepidermal nerve fiber density (IENFD) is the gold standard diagnostic test. In the context of leflunomide use and temporal correlation of symptom onset, leflunomide-induced small fiber neuropathy is the working diagnosis pending biopsy.

output.test_type: Skin Punch Biopsy — Intraepidermal Nerve Fiber Density (IENFD)

report.summary: Skin punch biopsy at proximal thigh (10 cm above iliac crest) and distal leg (10 cm above lateral malleolus). IENFD immunostaining with anti-PGP9.5 antibody.

results.distal_leg_IENFD: 2.1 fibers/mm (reference for age/sex: 7.4-12.2 fibers/mm) — MARKEDLY REDUCED, below 5th percentile
results.proximal_thigh_IENFD: 5.8 fibers/mm (reference for age/sex: 9.8-18.4 fibers/mm) — MODERATELY REDUCED, below 5th percentile
results.pattern: Length-dependent reduction (distal worse than proximal) — consistent with toxic/metabolic small fiber neuropathy
results.sweat_gland_innervation: Markedly reduced sweat gland nerve fiber density at distal leg

report.interpretation: SMALL FIBER NEUROPATHY CONFIRMED. IENFD severely reduced distally (2.1 fibers/mm vs reference >7.4) and moderately reduced proximally (5.8 fibers/mm) — length-dependent pattern consistent with toxic etiology. Leflunomide temporal correlation and exclusion of all other causes (diabetes negative, B12 normal, TSH normal, heavy metals negative, ANCA negative, no Sjögren's) makes LEFLUNOMIDE-INDUCED SMALL FIBER NEUROPATHY the diagnosis. Recommendation: discontinue leflunomide.

output.test_type: Autonomic Testing (QSART, Thermoregulatory Sweat Test, HRV)

report.summary: QSART bilateral feet: absent (0 uL, reference >0.40 uL). QSART bilateral legs: severely reduced. Thermoregulatory sweat test: absent sweating bilateral feet and lower legs (anhidrosis). HRV: mildly reduced. Orthostatic vitals: no orthostatic hypotension. Findings confirm severe postganglionic sudomotor failure (small fiber/autonomic neuropathy) in bilateral lower extremities.
report.interpretation: Severe autonomic small fiber involvement (sudomotor) in lower extremities — consistent with leflunomide-induced small fiber neuropathy. No orthostatic hypotension (cardiovascular autonomic fibers relatively spared).

report.summary: Corneal confocal microscopy: corneal nerve fiber density (CNFD) 14.2 fibers/mm² (reference 20-30 fibers/mm²) — REDUCED. Corneal nerve fiber length (CNFL) 8.4 mm/mm² (reference 14-25 mm/mm²) — REDUCED. Corneal nerve branch density (CNBD) 12.8 branches/mm² (reference 20-50) — REDUCED. Findings confirm small fiber neuropathy by corneal nerve measurement — consistent with skin biopsy findings. CCM is a non-invasive cross-validation.
report.interpretation: Corneal confocal microscopy corroborates skin biopsy IENFD findings — both demonstrate small fiber loss consistent with leflunomide-induced SFN. CCM can be used for non-invasive monitoring of SFN recovery during and after leflunomide washout.

report.summary: QST bilateral feet (standardized DFNS protocol): Warm Detection Threshold (WDT): markedly elevated bilateral feet (right 46.2°C, left 47.1°C; normal <40.5°C) — loss of warm perception. Cold Detection Threshold (CDT): elevated bilateral feet (right 26.8°C, left 25.4°C; normal >28.4°C) — loss of cold perception. Mechanical Pain Threshold (MPT): reduced (hyperalgesia to punctate stimuli) — 0.12 mN (normal 28-112 mN). Vibration Detection Threshold (VDT): NORMAL 4.8 Hz (normal <8 Hz) — large fiber intact.
report.interpretation: QST confirms SMALL FIBER NEUROPATHY: loss of thermal (warm and cold) detection with intact vibration detection threshold. Punctate hyperalgesia (reduced MPT) explains allodynia. Pattern: loss of A-delta (temperature) and C fiber (warm/pain) with preserved A-beta (vibration/touch) function — textbook small fiber neuropathy.

output.query: leflunomide peripheral neuropathy treatment small fiber

results.citation: Martin K et al. (2007) Peripheral neuropathy with leflunomide: a systematic review. Ann Rheum Dis 66:889-895.
results.summary: Leflunomide-associated peripheral neuropathy reported in 0.3-1% of patients; primarily axonal but small fiber cases reported; onset typically 6-24 months after initiation; reversible in 50-70% after discontinuation with cholestyramine washout; cases at therapeutic plasma levels document idiosyncratic mechanism.

results.citation: Bandyopadhyay D et al. (2020) Small fiber neuropathy from leflunomide: case series. J Neurol 267:1208-1214.
results.summary: Small fiber phenotype (normal large fiber NCS + reduced IENFD) documented in leflunomide neuropathy cases; cholestyramine washout accelerates drug elimination; 60% partial to complete pain improvement at 6 months post-discontinuation.

output.interpretation: Evidence supports leflunomide discontinuation with cholestyramine washout as primary treatment. Symptomatic treatment: duloxetine 60 mg daily (preferred — reduces central sensitization in SFN), pregabalin 75-150 mg twice daily (alternative), topical capsaicin 8% patch (for focal small fiber neuropathy), amitriptyline 10-25 mg nightly (sleep benefit). Duloxetine preferred over gabapentin in this patient with no comorbidities limiting its use.

critical_actions: Recognize small fiber neuropathy phenotype — normal NCS does NOT exclude neuropathy
Order skin punch biopsy for IENFD — standard NCS cannot diagnose SFN
Identify leflunomide as causative agent — temporal correlation is the key diagnostic clue
Discontinue leflunomide — recovery requires drug removal
Cholestyramine washout to accelerate leflunomide elimination (otherwise half-life is 15+ days due to enterohepatic recirculation)
Coordinate rheumatology for RA management after leflunomide cessation
contraindicated_actions: Do not dismiss as 'normal' because NCS is normal — small fiber neuropathy is invisible to standard NCS
Do not attribute to stress — prior neurologist's diagnosis was incorrect; structural skin biopsy test is objective
Do not discontinue methotrexate — leflunomide is the causative drug, not MTX
Do not start high-dose opioids as first-line — duloxetine and pregabalin are first-line for SFN pain

differential.key_distinguishing: Temporal correlation with leflunomide initiation makes idiopathic diagnosis inappropriate; drug rechallenge/dechallenge relationship supports causal role
HbA1c 5.2% — definitively no diabetes; glucose/fasting glucose normal
RA in clinical and serological remission (ESR 14, CRP 0.8, DAS28 1.8); RA neuropathy in remission would be improving not worsening; temporal correlation with leflunomide not RA activity
Anti-SSA/SSB negative; ANA 1:160 likely RA-related (context); no sicca symptoms; dry eye excluded by negative sicca workup

key_reasoning_points: MODERATE DIFFICULTY: Normal NCS labeled as 'negative workup' by prior neurologist — this is the classic pitfall in small fiber neuropathy
KEY PRINCIPLE: Standard NCS tests ONLY large myelinated A-beta fibers; C fibers and A-delta fibers (responsible for pain and temperature) are NOT assessed by NCS
SFN clinical phenotype: burning pain + allodynia + temperature loss + PRESERVED vibration/proprioception/reflexes — this combination points exclusively to small fibers
Leflunomide neuropathy: underrecognized drug toxicity; appears at therapeutic plasma levels; requires active cholestyramine washout due to enterohepatic recirculation
Overseas history, vaccinations, antimalarials, and dapsone exposure are all red herrings once heavy metals screen is negative
RA-related anti-CCP positivity and ANA 1:160 are expected findings and must not be over-interpreted as causal
